newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia court rejects Novolipetsk investor appeal.
newsitem.headline: Russia court rejects Novolipetsk investor appeal.

text.p: Investors in Russian steel mill Novolipetsk have suffered another setback in their struggle with company management for board representation, lawyers for the shareholders said on Monday.

A regional court rejected an appeal by Bank MFK (ICFI in English) against an earlier ruling that about five percent of its 15 percent stake in Novolipetsk was preferred and not voting stock, legal counsel Rafael Akopov said.

"On Friday, as was expected, the Lipetsk appeals court upheld the decision of its predecessor and the appeal was denied," said Akopov, also vice-president of Renaissance Capital, another minority shareholder fighting in Novolipetsk.

He said MFK would take the case, just one of a group of suits centering around the plant and being closely watched as a litmus test of the climate for foreign investment, to the Supreme Arbitration Court, seeking a reversal of both rulings.

AO Novolipetsky Metallurgichesky Kombinat (NLMK) is the largest steel mill in Europe, producing 3.46 million tonnes of rolled steel in the first half of 1997, up six percent on the same period a year ago.

The court defeat is the second for the group of investors, which also includes Cambridge Capital Management, who have battled with directors at Novolipetsk for months over failure to include their nominees on a slate of candidates to a new board.

Despite earlier court backing for the investors' demand that their candidates be put on the ballot, management failed to include voting for a new board on the agenda of the annual general meeting last month.
In the event, shareholders did not extend the current board's term as requested, promising to call an extraordinary shareholder meeting to vote in a new board.
But now the investors say even the court has turned against them, with the most recent rebuff casting an apparent shadow over the plans to call a new meeting.

Renaissance Capital, MFK and Cambridge Capital Management say they together hold a controlling stake in the Novolipetsk mill. Renaissance Capital and MFK, which is part of the Uneximbank group, are planning to merge.
